note: The Central Bank of Liberia's Automated Check Processing/Automated Clearing House (ACP)/(ACH) System Rules (version 1.2, 9 November 2017; the copy on the CBL's site, read 2026-10-30), Appendix A1 (Check and Account Number Standards), following the WAMZ specifications: the Basic Bank Account Number is codified over 18 positions, the bank's code (3 digits), the branch's (3), the account number (10, padded with zeros on the left) and the account check digit (2), the check being 97 less the remainder of 100 times the 16 digits before it divided by 97 (01 to 97), the French RIB's key, held as key97. The rules' worked check (bank 001, branch 001, account 0000000111, check 57) gives the example, 001001000000011157, which passes. The rules say the bank, state and branch codes are to be developed by the CBL on the WAMZ harmonized cheque specification; no code list was read. Liberia's two currencies (430 for the Liberian dollar, 840 for the US dollar) are a code on the cheque, not part of the BBAN.

sources.title: Central Bank of Liberia, Automated Check Processing/Automated Clearing House (ACP)/(ACH) System Rules (version 1.2, 9 November 2017)
sources.said: Account Number is ten digits which will be extracted from the customer account ... number. ... The assembly formed in order by the bank code, branch code and account number (either ... corporate or personal account number) constitutes a number (N) of 16 digits. ... Therefore, the rest of the following subtraction (97 – (N´ mod 97)) can only take values ... 001 001 0000000111 57 ... The Basic Bank Account Number (BBAN) is codified over 18 positions as follows: ... The bank code 03 Number Completed with 0 on the left ... The branch code 03 Number Completed with 0 on the left ... Account number 10 Number Completed with 0 on the left ... Account check digit 02 Number
